 Spencer Jones (hamstring) is out for Saturday’s game against the Pelicans. 
 The Nuggets aren’t going to take any chances with Jones, who’s working his way back from a strained hamstring. Rookie Trevon Brazile played 18 minutes off the bench in his debut and grabbed 12 rebounds. He’s likely to take on a similar role as Aaron Gordon’s backup on Saturday. 
 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #7 
 Trevon Brazile finished Thursday’s loss to the Thunder with four points (1-of-6 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs) and 12 rebounds. 
 In his official NBA debut, Brazile struggled from the field, missing all four of his three-point attempts. However, the second-round pick out of Arkansas was effective on the glass, leading the Nuggets with 12 rebounds. Brazile played 18 minutes, partly because Spencer Jones (hamstring) didn’t play. However, despite the perimeter shooting struggles, the rookie’s rebounding output was encouraging. 
 Spencer Jones 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #21 
 Spencer Jones (hamstring) is questionable for Thursday’s game against the Thunder. 
 Due to a strained left hamstring, Jones did not play at all during the preseason. He’s on the injury report for Denver’s season opener due to bilateral hamstring injury management, so his right hamstring is also a concern. If Jones can’t play, the Nuggets may have to rely on rookie Trevon Brazile a little more, with the second-round pick coming off a productive preseason. 
 Spencer Jones 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #21 
 Spencer Jones (hamstring) said on Sunday that he expects to be available for Thursday’s opener against the Thunder. 
 Jones strained his left hamstring early in training camp and did not play in any of the Nuggets’ preseason games. He’s made positive strides in his recovery, most recently doing some scrimmaging during Sunday’s practice. Following the session, Jones said that he expects to be available for Sunday’s opener. If Jones plays, there may be fewer minutes available to rookie Trevon Brazile, who played well in the Nuggets’ final preseason games. 
 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward-Center 
 Trevon Brazile amassed 12 points (5-of-7 FGs, 0-of-3 FTs), eight rebounds, two assists, two steals, two blocks and two three-pointers in Friday’s exhibition against the Lakers. 
 With Aaron Gordon sitting out Friday’s preseason finale, the Nuggets inserted Brazile into the starting lineup. The rookie, who dropped 22 points on Wednesday against the Clippers, had another solid outing to end his first preseason. Brazile may not play heavy minutes, but he’s clearly done enough to crack the Nuggets’ rotation right away. 
 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward-Center 
 Trevon Brazile amassed 22 points (8-of-10 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Clippers. 
 The 35th overall pick in this past summer’s draft, Brazile had his most productive night of the preseason on Wednesday. The 6-foot-10 forward/center shot 80 percent from the field, and his final line lacked only an assist. Based on playing time, Brazile has already leapfrogged former first-round picks Zeke Nnaji and DaRon Holmes II in the frontcourt pecking order. He may not get the minutes needed to impact fantasy basketball once the regular season begins, but Brazile needs to be rostered in dynasty leagues. 
 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward-Center 
 Trevon Brazile finished Sunday’s 109-97 loss to the Jazz with seven points, three rebounds, two blocked shots and a triple across 20 minutes. 
 The rookie out of Arkansas tied Julian Strawther for team lead in minutes, and he had a serviceable night, going 3-of-4 from the field and making an impact on defense. Denver doesn’t boast a deep bench, especially in the frontcourt, so Brazile has a real chance to earn meaningful rotation minutes in Year 1. 
 Spencer Jones 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #21 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Nuggets are matching the Thunder’s offer sheet, keeping Spencer Jones on a two-year contract. 
 The Nuggets’ decision to match the Thunder’s offer sheet comes less than 48 hours after OKC’s initial offer. Jones, who averaged 5.5 points and 3.3 rebounds across 64 games last regular season, should remain a solid piece off Denver’s bench for the 2026-27 campaign. He’s mostly a three-point specialist who can provide some perimeter defense as well during his minutes, but is unlikely to move high enough up Denver’s depth chart to have any fantasy value next season. 
 Spencer Jones 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #21 
 Spencer Jones has agreed to a two-year, $12 million offer sheet with the Thunder, reports NBA Insider Michael Scotto. 
 Jones is a restricted free agent, so the Nuggets still have the opportunity to match the contract and keep him. If not, this was a wise bit of maneuvering by the Thunder as they were able to offer Jones using the Taxpayer mid-level exception after getting under the second apron by trading Lu Dort. Jones averaged 5.5 points in 22.5 minutes per game during the regular season last year, but stepped up during the playoffs, shooting 69 percent from three-point range. 
 Trevon Brazile 
 DEN 
 Forward-Center 
 Trevon Brazile notched 17 points (6-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, one assist, three blocks and two three-pointers in Thursday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 Brazile did not have his best night shooting the basketball, but the second-round pick still showed why Denver made sure to draft him. Active on the glass and defensively, the 6-foot-10 forward finished with another solid stat line. Like fellow second-round pick Bryce Hopkins, Brazile has not yet agreed to a contract, with Peyton Watson’s free agency likely a factor. However, he has the potential to contribute immediately for the Nuggets because of his athleticism and motor.

 Grayson Allen provided a boost off the bench with 20 points (6-of-12 FGs), three rebounds, five assists, one steal and four three-pointers against the Heat on Saturday.
 Allen hasn’t started in place of Kon Knueppel (hamstring), but he has been able to fill the shooting void. That included a clutch four-point play in this game, which gave the Hornets a lead that they didn’t relinquish. Allen is rostered in just 33 percent of Yahoo! leagues, but with how many threes Charlotte shoots as a team, Allen should be rostered until Knueppel returns.

 Dennis Schröder lit up the Heat with 25 points (8-of-17 FGs), six rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers on Saturday.
 After struggling in Friday’s blowout loss to the Hawks, Schröder was able to bounce back with his best performance of the season. Two of his three starts in place of Coby White (calf) have been productive, with the one poor performance coming in a 47-point loss that was bad for the entire team. Schröder is worth streaming until White returns to the lineup. He’s currently rostered in just 26 percent of Yahoo! leagues.

 Brandon Miller led the Hornets with 34 points (10-of-29 FGs, 11-of-12 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one block and three three-pointers in a 115-110 win over the Heat on Saturday.
 Miller has been the focal point of the offense for Charlotte early on this year, which gives him a green light to shoot often. He is averaging 21.3 shot attempts per game this season, and while he still isn’t shooting efficiently, he was able to pour in the points in this one. The difference in this game was the free throw rate. He shot three total free throws in their first two games, far less than his 12 attempts in this one. Miller is going to continue to get as many shots as he wants until Kon Knueppel (hamstring) returns. He should be in for more big scoring nights, especially when his shot starts falling at a higher rate.

 Naz Reid lit up the Heat with 23 points (9-of-16 FGs), nine rebounds, two blocks and five three-pointers on Saturday.
 Reid has been productive in his first season as a Hornet, but this was his highest-scoring performance so far this year. It was also his best field goal percentage and the most triples he’s knocked down in a game this season. Reid has fit in flawlessly with Charlotte’s three-point heavy approach on offense, and he should continue to have some strong scoring nights. Any extra value he can add in other categories will just be a cherry on top.

 Davion Mitchell led the Heat with 22 points (8-of-13 FGs), one rebound, 10 assists, one steal and three three-pointers in a 15-110 loss to the Hornets on Saturday.
 Miami trailed by 21 points entering the fourth quarter, but Mitchell fueled a monster comeback, mostly with Giannis Antetokounmpo on the bench. That didn’t result in a win, but it was another strong performance for him. He has been fantastic this year, averaging 17.0 points, 8.7 assists and 2.3 three-pointers per game, all of which would be career bests for him. He has been a bright spot despite a rough start to the year for Miami.

 Pelle Larsson provided a boost off the bench with 15 points (5-of-9 FGs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer against the Hornets on Saturday.
 After a rough start to the year offensively, Larsson was able to get things going in this one. He totaled nine points on 1-of-9 shooting across his first two outings, so this performance was a huge step in the right direction. Larsson was a late-round flier for fantasy managers hoping he would take a step forward for the Heat this season. He’s trending in the right direction, but he’ll need to produce to this level more consistently to be worth keeping rostered.
